description.value: A cross-sectional study using high-dimensional pattern classification of volumetric MRI to distinguish Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia, and cognitively normal individuals.

spans.text: The purpose of this study is to determine the diagnostic accuracy of MRI-based high-dimensional pattern classification in differentiating between patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD), Frontotemporal Dementia (FTD), and healthy controls

description.value: Cross-sectional observational study of patients with Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia, and age-matched cognitively normal controls.

spans.text: To explore the advantage of this strategy, we conducted a cross-sectional study to determine if high-dimensional image analysis and pattern classification methods could be used to correctly identify individual patients with AD and FTD with high enough sensitivity and specificity to be clinically useful.
